subject: Vocabulary
topic: Word Formation — Prefixes, Suffixes and Roots in Context (W12 B1)

questions.stem: The prefix MIS- (as in 'misinterpret', 'misnomer', 'mischief') generally means:
questions.explanation: A is correct. MIS- = wrongly, badly, incorrectly. Misinterpret = interpret wrongly; misnomer = wrongly applied name; mischief = wrong conduct; mismanage = manage badly; misfortune = bad fortune. Trap: 'half or partial' = SEMI- or HEMI- (semicircle, hemisphere); 'together or jointly' = CO- or CON- (cooperate, conjoin); 'before or in advance' = PRE- (preview, predict). Note: MIS- should not be confused with MISS- (to fail to hit) — different word.

B is correct. -OLOGY = study of or science of (from Greek logos = word/reason/study). Examples: zoology (study of animals), psychology (study of mind), etymology (study of word origins), geology (study of the earth), ornithology (study of birds). Trap: 'fear of' = -PHOBIA (hydrophobia, claustrophobia); 'one who practises' = -IST or -ER (biologist, teacher); 'quality or state of' = -ITY or -NESS (purity, darkness).

B is correct. PRE- = before (Latin prae = before). Precaution = action taken before a problem (to prevent it); predecessor = one who came before; preemptive = acting before the opponent can; predict = say before it happens; prehistoric = before recorded history. Trap: POST- = after (postwar, postpone); ANTI- = against (antidote, anti-social); ULTRA- or TRANS- = beyond (ultraviolet, transcend).

options.option_text: a person who practises or advocates
the quality or state of something

questions.explanation: B is correct. -IST = a person who does, believes in, or is skilled in something. Pianist = one who plays the piano; protagonist = the main actor in a story (leading person); antagonist = one who opposes (opposing person); journalist = one who practises journalism; socialist = one who advocates socialism. Trap: 'belief or doctrine' = -ISM (socialism, Buddhism — the belief system itself); 'quality or state' = -ITY or -NESS (hostility, softness); 'act or process' = -TION or -MENT (creation, movement).

questions.stem: The prefix RE- (as in 'reconsider', 'reinforce', 'revive') primarily means:
questions.explanation: C is correct. RE- = again or back (Latin re- = again). Reconsider = consider again; reinforce = strengthen again; revive = bring back to life; return = turn back; rebuild = build again; recall = call back. Trap: 'away from' = DE- (detach, depart) or AB- (abduct, abnormal); 'between or among' = INTER- (international, interrupt); 'not or without' = UN- (unclear), IN- (incomplete), DIS- (disagree).

questions.stem: What does the suffix -FUL indicate in words like 'grateful', 'masterful', 'fanciful'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. -FUL = full of, characterised by, or having the quality of. Grateful = full of gratitude; masterful = having the quality of a master; fanciful = characterised by fancy/imagination; hopeful = full of hope; beautiful = full of beauty. Contrast with -LESS = without (hopeless, tasteless). Trap: 'without or lacking' = -LESS (hopeless, powerless); 'able to be' = -ABLE or -IBLE (readable, credible); 'one who' = -ER, -OR, -IST.

B is correct. UN- = not, or the reverse/opposite of. Unprecedented = without precedent (no prior example); unambiguous = not ambiguous; undaunted = not deterred or discouraged; unhappy = not happy; undo = reverse an action. Trap: 'excessively' = OVER- (overestimate, overdo); 'under or below' = UNDER- (undermine, underestimate) — note UNDER ≠ UN; 'one or single' = UNI- (unicycle, uniform) — note UNI ≠ UN.

questions.stem: The Latin root SCRIB/SCRIP (as in 'scribe', 'scripture', 'manuscript') means:
questions.explanation: B is correct. SCRIB/SCRIP = to write (Latin scribere = to write). Scribe = one who copies texts; scripture = sacred writings; manuscript = hand-written document (manu = hand + scrip = write); inscription = writing carved or engraved; prescription = written medical order (pre = before + scrip = write); describe = to write about. Trap: 'to speak' = DICT or VOC (dictate, vocal); 'to read' = LECT or LEG (lecture, legible); 'to draw' = GRAPH (photography, paragraph).

questions.stem: The prefix EX- (as in 'expatriate', 'explicit', 'exacerbate') most commonly means:
questions.explanation: C is correct. EX- = out of, from, or former (Latin ex = out of). Expatriate = one who lives outside their native country (ex = out of + patria = homeland); explicit = fully expressed and set out (nothing hidden — brought OUT); exacerbate = to make worse (ex + acerbus = bitter, intensifying 'out' from a state). As 'former': ex-president, ex-wife. Trap: INTRA- = inside/within (intravenous, intramural); INTER- = between (international, interim); TRANS- = across/through (transcontinental, transport). Note: EX- in 'exacerbate' acts as an intensifier, not 'out of' literally — making this a HARD distinction.

questions.stem: Which of the following compound words correctly follows the 'self + adjective/noun' pattern AND is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: C is correct. SELF-SUFFICIENT = able to supply one's own needs without outside help. The correct spelling uses: one hyphen (self-), double f (suf-ficient), -ient ending (not -ant or -ent variant). Common spelling errors: single f (suficient), -ent (selfsufficent), or no hyphen. Self- compounds use a hyphen: self-sufficient, self-confident, self-reliant, self-made. Trap: 'self-suficient' = one f missing (the f in 'suf-' belongs to the Latin prefix sub- assimilated before f, so 'suffix' not 'sufix'); no-hyphen form = accepted in some dictionaries but not the standard tested form in SSC.
